chapter: California, New York and Richard Himber
title: Recording and films with Prima, the Famous Door and meeting Himber
summary: The Prima band personnel, the film Start Cheering, the Famous Door in New York and how Richard Himber came to hear Hirsch there.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Who did you first record with?
Who did I first record with?
I think it was Louis, I think it was.

I think it was with Louis. Uh, with Louis Prima. And, uh, we did, uh, several pictures out there while I was with Louis. We did one with, uh, Start Cheering. They had everything but a kitchen sink in it. They had, they were, they used all contract plans. I mean, they'd have, uh, Cab Calloway, Gene Autry, uh, who and what? Forty-two people. I got, I got pictures of it in the books.
Who was on the band with you?

Uh, on the band was out there with Louis, was Louis Macenta on bass. I was playing drums and vibes. Frank Pinero was playing piano. Louis played trumpet. Frank Federico played guitar. Edmire Weinberg played, or Gene Mahath played clarinet. He was a very good clarinet player. He was a very legitimate player. Good jazz player, too. So, uh, then we came, left, we left, uh, we left, uh, we left Cal, uh, left California. And we came back here and we played for about a week. Where Pete Fountains Club used to be, which is now burned down. We were here for a week during the Christmas holidays and then we left right after that. And then we went to New York. And we went to the famous door. And we were supposed to be there for, I think, two or three weeks, but we stayed there till April. We had a piano player there by the name of Art Tatum. Fair piano player. Fair piano player. Fair piano player. He was responsible. So when I was there, Richard Himber and his lawyer came into the club one night. And Adrian Orlini was leaving Richard to go in to have his own trio and work at the President Hotel. And, uh, himber needed a bi-player. And he heard me and, uh, he came in one night with his, uh, with his attorney, Andrew Weinberger, who was also Tommy Darcy's director and board attorney. And, uh, one of the waiters came up to me and said, After you finish, there's a man over there who wants to talk to you. I said, alright. So when I went afterwards, I went over and said, yes sir. So Andrew got up and he says, my name's Andrew Weinberger. He says, uh, no, Dick came over. Dick came over to me. Dick came over. He says, uh, this is Mr. Andrew Weinberger. Sit down here, I want to talk to you. And he's a very crude, Dick's a very crude guy to begin with. Uh, can you play with Bull Mallets?
